note: v1 93.72 (seeds 0/11 93.72/93.70), first draft of SOULFUL DEEP HOUSE, 'One More Step', for The Endless Stair - featured illusion THE SPEECH-TO-SONG ILLUSION. A spoken phrase, 'one more step up', repeats every two bars over a warm deep groove (machine-kit, sub, Rhodes on Em9 - Cmaj9 - Am9 - Bm7). At first it is plainly speech, a conversational falling contour; through the second section its contour is pulled, repetition by repetition, onto THE STAIR (E F# G B, the tape's thread) until the sentence sings; a sung double surfaces under it, the break leaves the song alone with a filtered Rhodes, the Rhodes quotes the stair in the last groove, and in the outro the plain speech returns - which by then the ear can only hear as melody. Tempo ramps 118.5 -> 119 inside the track (the mix plan's path); seams drafted with t2 and t4 in mixplan.md. 4:53.

v2 93.74 (seeds 0/11 93.74/93.72, level with v1 93.72/93.70): THE TAPE'S LEVEL. One More Step sat at -12.7 LUFS while its neighbours run at -11 (chirper-zero's recipe, Which Ear), which in a continuous mix is a 1.7 LU dip at both seams. Its own master chain now hands over to the song's loudness stage at -11.0 LUFS (true peak -1.29 dBTP, levels 100 on both seeds), so it sits level in the tape. (Swapping the whole chain for the -15 dB / 8:1 recipe instead squashed the sections together on seed 11 - returns 72 - so the chain stays and only the final loudness changes.)

v3 97.45 (seeds 0/11 97.45/97.42, level with v2 re-scored under rhythm 0.03): the tape-wide seam fix from The Ghost Note. The song now ends on its last bar (tail 0.1 s, no length padding) instead of 1.5 s of padding plus release, so the outro's last bars are what a DJ mixes into t4. No change to the music.

v4 91.28 (seeds 0/11 91.28/91.42 vs v3 re-scored with t2 and t4 now present, 92.54/92.51): mixed for the DJ seam, kept on judgment. Now that the groove overlaps neighbours for 16 bars, v3's intro put a full-range kick over t2's from bar 4: two kicks fighting in the low end. Now One More Step does what a DJ does: a BASS SWAP. Its intro kick is high-passed at 110 Hz from bar 1 (t2 keeps the low end under the overlap; closed hats only), the low Em pad and open hats arrive at bar 9, and the full kick lands together with the bass on A's downbeat - so the low end changes hands on a downbeat instead of doubling. B lifts with a ride on every off-beat and a cowbell ghost where the speech starts to sing. And the tempo ramp now runs between the seams (chirper-zero's finding): 118.5 held through the intro, 119 through the outro, so neither overlap flams. Score: the join from t2 improves 13.6 -> 6.4 dB, but compscore's edge measure can't hear the overlap, and the thinner intro costs 1.3 on recurrence and flow spectra.

v5 93.81 (seeds 0/11 93.81/93.83 vs v4 re-scored 91.28/91.42): THE SWAP AT THE MIDPOINT. chirper-three measured that a bass swap at the incoming track's bar 17 leaves a hole in the live mix: the groove's crossfade is linear, so the outgoing lows fade towards nothing while the incoming ones wait. v4 swapped at bar 17 - and measured on the real crossfade of t2's last 16 bars and t3's first 16 (low-passed at 120 Hz, RMS per bar) its lows sagged 13.3 dB to a hole at bar 13. Now the swap lands at bar 9, the overlap's midpoint, where both sides are at half level: the full kick and an E sub take over there, with the Em pad and open hats. Measured: the lows hold within 5.9 dB across the whole overlap (std 4.6 -> 1.5 dB) and run straight into A at the same level. compscore likes it too: one intro section fewer, recurrence back to 100.

v6 94.64 (seeds 0/11 94.64/94.69 vs v5 re-scored 93.75/93.76): the Em floor from bar 1. Now that the live mix swaps the lows at the overlap's midpoint itself (swap mid on t2 -> t3), One More Step's low Em pad can return to the intro's first bar: it gives t2's open A-E fifth an E-minor floor to land on through the whole overlap, instead of eight bars of thin kick and closed hats alone. The thin kick still hands to the full kick and E sub at bar 9, the same midpoint as the mixer. Flow from t2 52 -> 58 (spectral 11.9 -> 6.8 dB).

v7 94.71 (seeds 0/11 94.71/94.66, level with v6 re-scored 94.63/94.68): ONE MORE STEP UP. The brief asks each track to play with time, tone and key around its illusion; One More Step played with time (118.5 -> 119) and with tone (speech becoming song) but sat in E minor throughout. Now the last groove takes the phrase at its word: on C's downbeat, after the break where the sung double is alone, the whole song steps up a tone, E minor to F# minor - the bass, the Rhodes, the pad, the sung double, the stair quote an octave up - and stays there through the outro, where the plain speech returns a tone higher than it began. F#m hands to t4's Bm as a neighbour on the wheel (11A -> 10A), so the seam still sits right; mixplan updated. Kept on judgment: compscore is level, the song now has a lift it didn't have.

v8 96.01 (seeds 0/11 96.01/95.95 vs v7 re-scored 94.71/94.66): presence for the voice. One More Step's 2.6-4.2 kHz sat 6-10 dB under the tape - exactly where speech becomes intelligible and a sung line gets its air - while 290-550 Hz ran 6 dB heavy. The master now lifts 3.3 kHz by 5 dB and dips 300 Hz by 3 (from 2), so the spoken phrase reads as words and the sung double has air above the Rhodes; the hats get crisper with it (compscore's rhythm term hears the sixteenths better: 87 -> 94). Spectrum 92 -> 99+.

v9 96.18 (seeds 0/11 96.18/96.11 vs v8 re-scored 96.01/95.95): THE LONG TURN - against repetition, and for the illusion. One More Step leaves the shared template too: the first groove shortens to 24 bars and the second grows to 40, so the spoken phrase now repeats for 32 bars of B while its contour slides onto THE STAIR (it reached song after 24 before), with the sung double joining at B's bar 21. The speech-to-song illusion is built on repetition - the more times the ear hears the same words, the more it hears a tune - so the turn is now slower and surer. The break, the key step-up at C and both seams sit where they were (same bars, same length). Four of my five tracks are now off the template; Both Ways keeps it.

v10 95.67 (seeds 0/11 95.67/95.61, level with v9 re-scored with chirper-zero's new 9.0, 95.73/95.68): THE PROOF, from chirper-zero's rating note - let the plain speech stand alone so each listener can test their own ears. His suggestion was the outro's last repeats; I tried it (no drums or pad under bars 9-12) and it cost 4.7 (returns 100 -> 67), and in the live mix those bars sit under t4's incoming head anyway, so they can never be alone. The break can: its first eight bars now give the phrase back as PLAIN SPEECH - the spoken contour, unquantised - alone over the pad, right after 32 bars of repetitions; if it still sings, the illusion is proved in the listener's own ear. The sung double answers in the break's last eight bars, then the key steps up. Kept on judgment: level within the seed spread.

v11 95.79 (seeds 0/11 95.79/95.78 vs v10 re-scored 95.70/95.65): darker chords and the illusion from the first groove's first bar, for Harry's 31 Oct steers. The progression goes from Em9 - Cmaj9 - Am9 - Bm7 (the 'too-basic' kind: a plain major ninth and a minor dominant) to Em11 - Cmaj7#11 - Am9 - B7b9 - a minor second hidden in the Em11 and the Cmaj7#11, and a real dominant with a flat ninth pulling home (and, after the step up, the same colours in F# minor). The spoken phrase now starts on the first groove's first bar instead of its ninth: chirpers.py illusion (speech + sung) near the front for 87% of the track (from 81%), longest stretch without 30 s (from 46) - only the seam intro is bare, by design (it sits under t2's tail). Not heard by me.

v12 95.73 (seeds 0/11 95.73/95.72, level with v11 95.79/95.78): THE STEP RISER, for Harry's 31 Oct steer ('much harder on time-play ... accelerating fills, risers'). In the break's last bar - after eight bars of the plain spoken phrase alone and eight of the sung double - the word 'step' stutters fourteen times, each gap 0.82 of the one before (an accelerating fill that crams the bar), climbing the stair from E3 up to D5, and lands on the downbeat where the whole song steps up a tone into F# minor. The riser is built from the phrase itself: speech turning into rhythm on its way to becoming a key change. Kept on judgment: level within the seed spread. Not heard by me.
